overview: Extends the Phase 1 Layercake membership solution so that every membership event (Join, Change, Lapse, Readmission, Renewal) can be segmented by payment method, payer type and concession type, every Join, Renewal and Readmission can carry its contact-year's invoiced amount in GBP, and Practising / Retired is set from a retirement date derived from retired concessions (AMD-001). Subscription invoices, invoice lines, corporate subscriptions and the concession reference are landed 1:1 in bronze from objects other systems own, and the Phase 1 brnz_subs_status gains 'Inv Total Amount' and 'Retired Concession' from Subs.vwSubsMemberStatuses. Invoice lines are landed at the source's ledger-distribution grain, one row per (recid, postingtype, accountdisplayvalue), and every reader takes a transaction's settled amount once per transaction (AMD-002, ADR-006). Silver adds the segment reference lists, an item-code line-type mapping, a currency list and one attributes row per contact per Campaign Year, set from each year's segment invoice. It adds silv_event_amount, which places each contact-year's Inv Total Amount on one event and pairs each event with its own eligible invoice for the invoice checks only, and ten new anomaly types in the existing silv_data_anomaly. A new view derives each contact's retirement date from brnz_subs_status, and the Phase 1 silv_member_base load takes it in place of apuk_retirementdate (ADR-005), so in Phase 1 only results split by membership status change. Four new gold dimensions are added, and the existing silver and gold event tables carry the segment keys, carried flags, subs_amount_gbp, invoiced_subtotal_gbp and amount_status. The daily load is made accurate (AMD-003). On every run, the Phase 1 daily count finds the past dates whose silver inputs changed by comparing the inputs with a stored basis (ADR-007). It recomputes them from 2020-10-01 onward and writes only the differences, so stored daily history always equals a full rebuild. Each change to a date already loaded is recorded in the new Layercake.silv_daily_count_adjustment. Two table functions give the figures as known at any time, and a view lists the adjustments for review (ADR-008). The daily load is then made faster without changing its results (AMD-006). Each measure is counted as the sum of per-contact contributions, guarded by a check that no contact holds overlapping state ranges. A normal run recomputes only the contacts whose inputs changed: it takes out each one's contribution as last applied, worked out from a snapshot of its inputs, and adds its new one (ADR-011). @FullRebuild, @RebuildFrom, a changed reference table and recovery from a run that did not finish still recompute the whole spine. The gold fact_daily_member_count_detail is synced cell by cell, and its id is widened to bigint. The daily counts then gain the three segments (AMD-007): silv_daily_count_detail, its adjustment history, its cell counts, the detail as-known-at function, the review view and fact_daily_member_count_detail add payment_method_id, payer_type_id and concession_type_id to their grain, taken from each contact's attributes for the Campaign Year of the day, while silv_daily_count and every total at the old grain are unchanged. Layercake.usp_run_daily_load runs the segment loads (usp_run_payment_segments, ADR-001) under the same run_id after the Phase 1 gold step and holds the daily count and the gold daily fact back until after them, so one call populates everything and the daily count uses the same run's attributes (ADR-012). The first run after that change is deployed restates stored daily history at the new grain without recording the change of grain as an adjustment (ADR-013). Subs.vwCorpSubscriptions is at subscription-user grain, so a corporate subscription key can repeat: the bronze load lands one copy per key in a fixed order, logs how many source rows it did not land, and does not fail on a repeat (AMD-004, ADR-009, ADR-010). Members' country and region then follow their local group (AMD-008, REQ-027). CE.vwLocalGroup is landed at local group grain beside the unchanged Phase 1 country-grain landing (ADR-014). A local group list and dimension are added, and one view decides each member's local group, country and regions, falling back wholly to the member's own country where the group cannot give them (ADR-016, provisional under Q-068). The existing country and region fields carry the local group's values on every date, closed Campaign Years included. The member's own country and its region are kept as contact_country_id and contact_region, and local_group_id and contact_country_id join the grain of the daily counts and the annual rate base. Gold reaches the group's region through the unchanged country_id and dim_country, which gains a row for each country and region combination a group needs (ADR-015), so Power BI needs no change. The first run after deployment restates stored daily history at the local group values without recording the move as adjustments (Q-067). Count-only profiling, coverage, retirement and employer findings queries are delivered as read-only procedures (ADR-003). Employer segmentation is findings only, so no employer objects are created. Every change ships as a framework migration with a tested down script, all objects live in the Layercake schema, and names follow the Phase 1 conventions.

layers.name: bronze
layers.purpose: brnz_* tables: 1:1 landings of external sources (Subs.tblSubsInvoices, synapse_fo.CUSTTRANS_RICS at its ledger-distribution grain, Subs.vwCorpSubscriptions, CE.vwConcessionType) with the standard bronze audit columns and soft delete, and the Phase 1 brnz_subs_status (Subs.vwSubsMemberStatuses) extended with inv_total_amount and retired_concession. From AMD-008 Layercake.brnz_local_group_detail lands CE.vwLocalGroup at local group grain beside the unchanged country-grain brnz_local_group (ADR-014), and the Phase 1 brnz_contact gains rics_localgroupid. No value transformation and no aggregation.

layers.name: silver
layers.purpose: silv_* tables and views: segment reference lists with reserved ids, the line-type mapping, the currency list, the eligible-invoice view, silv_member_year_attributes, silv_event_amount, the derived retirement date view, the new columns on the existing silv_membership_events, anomaly rows in the existing silv_data_anomaly, and the derived date held in the existing silv_member_base.retirement_date. The Phase 1 daily counts (silv_daily_count_detail, silv_daily_count) are corrected for every changed past date on every run. From AMD-007 silv_daily_count_detail carries payment_method_id, payer_type_id and concession_type_id in its grain, from the attributes of each day's Campaign Year, while silv_daily_count keeps its grain. silv_daily_count_adjustment holds their adjustment history at the detail grain, read through the as-known-at functions and the adjustments review view. From AMD-008 silv_ref_local_group and silv_ref_country_region hold the local groups and the country and region combinations they need, vw_silv_contact_local_group decides each member's local group, country and regions, and the member base, member profile, state ranges, events, daily counts and annual rate base carry the local-group country and region with local_group_id, contact_country_id and, where region is stored, contact_region.

layers.name: gold
layers.purpose: dim_payment_method, dim_payer_type, dim_currency and dim_concession_type copied from silver, and the new keys, flags and GBP amount measures on the existing fact_membership_events. fact_annual_rate_base keeps its segment-free grain (Q-007); its Practising / Retired split changes through the Phase 1 load (REQ-017). fact_daily_member_count_detail is synced from silver cell by cell and its id is widened from int to bigint (REQ-025). From AMD-007 it gains payment_method_id, payer_type_id and concession_type_id in its grain, holding the dim_payment_method, dim_payer_type and dim_concession_type keys, so a report needs to sum over them to get the old grain (REQ-026). From AMD-008 dim_local_group is added, dim_country gains the country and region combination rows (ADR-015), and fact_daily_member_count_detail, fact_membership_events and fact_annual_rate_base gain local_group_id and contact_country_id, with country_id pointing at the dim_country row that gives the member's region by local group (REQ-027).

layers.name: reporting queries
layers.purpose: usp_profile_* and usp_report_* read-only procedures that return aggregates only (counts, sums, rates) for profiling, coverage, retirement comparison and employer findings.

layers.name: load logging
layers.purpose: Every load records start, row counts and outcome in Layercake.etl_run_log through the existing Layercake.usp_etl_log_start and Layercake.usp_etl_log_end (project override of base standards 3). The Phase 1 daily count control tables etl_daily_count_loaded and etl_daily_count_pending_rebuild stay; the pending-rebuild table becomes a diagnostic only. etl_daily_count_input_basis is added to hold the daily count's silver inputs as last applied (ADR-007). From AMD-006 it is joined by the snapshot tables etl_daily_count_applied_contact, etl_daily_count_applied_state_range, etl_daily_count_applied_payment and etl_daily_count_applied_event, and by etl_daily_count_cell_contacts (ADR-011). From AMD-007 etl_daily_count_applied_attribute holds each contact's attributes as last applied, and etl_daily_count_cell_contacts carries the three segment columns. From AMD-008 the snapshot also holds each contact's local group, own country and own-country region as last applied, and etl_daily_count_input_basis holds a 'local_group_restatement' marker until the first run after deployment completes. The daily count logs its contacts recomputed and its path as etl_progress_log sub-steps.

entities.description: Lands the RULE-077 scope of synapse_fo.CUSTTRANS_RICS into brnz_subs_invoice_line at the source's grain, one row per source row (RULE-104). MOD-019 changes it to match source rows to bronze on (recid, postingtype, accountdisplayvalue). A null matches a null, and strings are compared under the database collation, as the unique index compares them. It inserts new rows; updates rows whose values differ, including the five ledger columns, and refreshes _updated_at; soft-deletes rows gone from the source; and restores rows that reappear. Unchanged rows are untouched, so a rerun on unchanged source logs 0 inserted, 0 updated and 0 deleted, and a change to one row of a split transaction updates that row only. Two source rows in scope with the same identity fail the load: it logs Failed, re-raises and leaves the target unchanged, and no row is skipped. The row-count check (live rows equal the source rows in scope) and the logging are unchanged. Rows landed before the change hold null in the new columns, so the first run after deployment soft-deletes them and inserts the source rows at the new grain. The exception is a source row whose postingtype and accountdisplayvalue are also both null: that row matches its old row and is updated. The down script restores the MOD-002 definition.

entities.name: Layercake.usp_load_brnz_corporate_subscription
entities.description: Lands Subs.vwCorpSubscriptions into brnz_corporate_subscription with the standard insert, update, soft-delete and restore behaviour and logging. MOD-024 changed it (REQ-022) and MOD-025 changes it again (REQ-023). A source row with a NULL Contact No or Scheme No still fails the load with error 515, whether or not its Sub Campaign Year is NULL: it logs Failed, re-raises and leaves the target unchanged (RULE-130, RULE-137). A source row with a NULL Sub Campaign Year is not landed and does not fail the load. Its Campaign Year is never derived or guessed, it takes no part in choosing the copy of a repeated key and it is not counted as a repeat (RULE-134). The source rows that have a Sub Campaign Year are reduced to one copy per key, chosen by the four steps of the corporate subscription repeated keys pattern (RULE-128, ADR-009), and bronze is compared with those copies. So a key whose source rows all lose their Sub Campaign Year is soft-deleted like any row missing from the source, and a row whose Sub Campaign Year is later set is landed by the next run with no manual step (RULE-138). Neither a repeated key nor a missing Campaign Year is an error, and neither writes a silv_data_anomaly row (RULE-129, RULE-136). The row-count check compares the number of distinct keys among the source rows that have a Sub Campaign Year with the live bronze rows (RULE-130). Every run that passes the key check writes two Layercake.etl_progress_log sub-steps under the load's log_id, in the way ADR-010 decides: 'repeated_key_rows_not_landed', with rows_affected set to the source rows that have a Sub Campaign Year minus their distinct keys (RULE-129); and 'no_campaign_year_rows_not_landed', with rows_affected set to the source rows whose Sub Campaign Year is NULL (RULE-135). Each is 0 when nothing applies. A run that fails on a NULL Contact No or Scheme No writes neither. Because the chosen copy depends only on the source data, a rerun on unchanged source logs 0 inserted, 0 updated and 0 deleted. The table's structure, its readers and usp_run_payment_segments are unchanged. MOD-025's down script restores the MOD-024 definition.

entities.name: Layercake.silv_daily_count_adjustment
entities.description: Adjustment history of the daily counts (REQ-019). There is one row per daily count cell per run that changed any of the cell's seven measures. The cell is the grain of silv_daily_count_detail: [date], region, country_id, gender_id, grade, membership_status_id and, from AMD-007, payment_method_id, payer_type_id and concession_type_id (RULE-155). Each row holds new minus old for each measure. A cell missing on either side counts as 0 (RULE-113). A measure the run did not change holds 0, and a check constraint rejects a row whose seven changes are all 0. The first load of a date never loaded before writes no row. Every later change writes one: repeat loads of today, corrections of past dates, and manual @RebuildFrom and @FullRebuild calls (RULE-114, RULE-115). Rows are written in the same transaction as the change they record, so a rolled-back change leaves no row (RULE-116). The table is insert-only: no load updates or deletes a row, and nothing purges it (RULE-117). grade holds the silver grades ('enrolment', 'election', 'lapse'), as silv_daily_count_detail does. Unique on (run_id, [date], region, country_id, gender_id, grade, membership_status_id, payment_method_id, payer_type_id, concession_type_id). MOD-028 adds the three segment columns through a change script and sets them to -2 Not applicable on every row written before deployment, keeping those rows' figures, run_id, load_id and written_at (RULE-162). The restatement run after deployment records its changes at the old grain with -2 in the three columns (ADR-013, Q-061). Every later row carries its cell's actual ids (AC-026-10). MOD-031 adds local_group_id, contact_country_id and contact_region (RULE-176) through a change script and widens the unique key to the run and the twelve grain columns. Every row written before deployment keeps its run_id, load_id, written_at, date, existing grain columns and seven changes, and takes contact_country_id equal to its country_id, contact_region equal to its region and local_group_id -2 Not applicable (Q-067 answer; RULE-179 and AC-027-13 say 0, Q-068). The restatement run records its real changes in the same form (restatement by local group pattern). Every later row carries its cell's actual values. -2 appears in local_group_id only here and in the as-known-at function and review view, never in a stored daily count or in gold.

entities.name: Layercake.fn_silv_daily_count_detail_as_known_at
entities.description: Table function giving the daily counts as known at a time, at the detail grain (ADR-008, RULE-119 to RULE-121). Parameters: @date_from date and @date_to date, both inclusive, and @as_known_at datetime2(3). If any parameter is NULL, no rows are returned. It returns one row per detail cell in the date range that has a stored row in silv_daily_count_detail or an adjustment written after @as_known_at. Each of the seven figures is the stored figure (0 where the cell has no stored row) minus the sum of that cell's changes in silv_daily_count_adjustment written strictly after @as_known_at. A change written exactly at @as_known_at is part of the figure (Q-049). A cell with no stored row whose seven figures all come to 0 is not returned. A date first loaded after @as_known_at returns its first-load figures (Q-050). With @as_known_at after the latest adjustment, it returns exactly the stored rows. MOD-028 changes it to the AMD-007 detail grain (RULE-155): payment_method_id, payer_type_id and concession_type_id follow membership_status_id in the result and in the cell match, taken from the stored cell and the adjustment rows. Its parameters and rules are otherwise unchanged. Adjustment rows written before deployment, and by the restatement run, carry -2, so for a time before deployment the figures are exact summed over the three columns, but are not split by segment, and a -2 cell can show figures that only add up when summed (RULE-163). MOD-031 adds local_group_id, contact_country_id and contact_region after concession_type_id, in the result and in the cell match, taken from the stored cell and the adjustment rows (RULE-176). Rows written before that deployment carry their own country and region in the contact columns and -2 in local_group_id, so for a time before it the figures are exact by own country and wherever region, country_id and local_group_id are summed over, but not split by the local group's region or country (RULE-179).

With @as_known_at after the latest adjustment, it equals silv_daily_count on these columns (AC-020-03, AC-020-09). entities.name: Layercake.etl_daily_count_input_basis
entities.description: Control table for the daily count correction (ADR-007): the daily count's silver inputs as last applied. It holds one row per contact with daily count inputs (input_name 'contact', input_key = contact_no). It also holds one row per reference table the Phase 1 daily derivation reads (input_name = the table name, input_key empty). The fingerprint covers only the rows and columns the derivation reads. Changes to segment and amount columns on events, and to load audit columns, are therefore not input changes (AC-019-08). For ref_date_spine and ref_campaign_year_config it covers only the rows up to the latest loaded date, so the daily extension of the spine is not a change (RULE-147, Q-058). From AMD-007 a contact's fingerprint also covers its silv_member_year_attributes rows (campaign_year, payment_method_id, payer_type_id and concession_type_id; not the carried flags, corporate_account_ref, segment_invoice_rec_id or audit columns), so a change to any of the three ids makes it a changed contact (RULE-160). silv_ref_payment_method, silv_ref_payer_type and silv_ref_concession_type are not reference inputs (RULE-161). MOD-028's migration writes one marker row, input_name 'detail_grain_restatement' with input_key empty and earliest_affected_date 2020-10-01, meaning stored history is not yet restated at the segment grain; the final transaction of the first run that completes removes it (ADR-013). Only usp_load_silv_daily_count writes the table otherwise, and only in a run's final transaction, after every batch of the run has committed. Changed rows are updated, new ones inserted, and rows whose input has gone are deleted. From MOD-026 that final transaction also writes the snapshot tables, so a contact's basis row and its etl_daily_count_applied_* rows always describe the same inputs (ADR-011). Structure unchanged by AMD-006, AMD-007 and AMD-008. The table was empty after MOD-022's deployment, so its first run recomputed every date from 2020-10-01 (RULE-109).

entities.name: Layercake.usp_load_silv_daily_count
entities.description: Existing Phase 1 daily count load, called by usp_load_silver in the silver step after the member profile, and since MOD-029 by usp_run_daily_load after usp_run_payment_segments (ADR-012). It is changed by MOD-022, MOD-026, MOD-028 and MOD-031. The Phase 1 rule for which contacts are counted, and what each contributes, is unchanged throughout. MOD-022: every run compares the inputs with etl_daily_count_input_basis, finds the earliest affected date (ADR-007) and recomputes every date from there to today, in date-ordered batches. It writes differences only, with one silv_daily_count_adjustment row per changed detail cell of a date already marked loaded. MOD-026 makes three changes. (1) Every path counts each of the seven measures as the sum of the contacts' contributions (daily count form pattern, RULE-144, RULE-146). (2) Before anything is written, every path checks that no contact holds two overlapping non-zero-length state ranges. If one does, the load fails with a clear error naming the contact and writes nothing (RULE-145). (3) A normal run takes the changed-contacts path (ADR-011). It applies only the contacts whose inputs changed since they were last applied. For each, it takes out the contribution worked out from its snapshot in the etl_daily_count_applied_* tables and adds the contribution from its current inputs, on the loaded dates either reaches. Dates not yet loaded are first-loaded from all contacts. These take the full-recompute path, which is the MOD-022 behaviour from 2020-10-01 or the computed start: @FullRebuild, @RebuildFrom, a changed reference input (RULE-147), and a snapshot not in step with the basis (after deployment, or after a run that did not finish). Both paths commit date-ordered batches, each with its adjustment rows, etl_daily_count_loaded marks and etl_daily_count_cell_contacts changes. Both end by bringing the basis and the snapshot into line in one final transaction. Every run that passes the guard logs the etl_progress_log sub-steps 'contacts_recomputed' and 'full_recompute_path' (RULE-153). Covered open etl_daily_count_pending_rebuild rows are marked applied as before. MOD-028 makes three further changes (REQ-026). (4) On every path each contact-day sits in the cell of its silv_member_year_attributes row for the day's Campaign Year, which adds payment_method_id, payer_type_id and concession_type_id to the cell, 0 where there is no row (daily count segment grain pattern). (5) A contact's inputs, fingerprint and snapshot also cover its attributes rows, held in etl_daily_count_applied_attribute, so an attribute change alone makes it a changed contact on the normal path; the three segment reference lists are not inputs (RULE-160, RULE-161). (6) While the 'detail_grain_restatement' marker is in etl_daily_count_input_basis, the run takes the full path from 2020-10-01, writes every loaded date at the new grain and records adjustments at the old grain; its final transaction removes the marker (restatement at the segment grain pattern, ADR-013). MOD-031 makes three more (REQ-027). (7) On every path each contact-day's cell also carries the contact's local_group_id and contact_country_id from silv_member_profile and contact_region from silv_member_state_ranges, beside country_id and region, which now carry the local-group values (member country and region by local group pattern). (8) A contact's inputs, fingerprint and snapshot cover those values, held in etl_daily_count_applied_contact and etl_daily_count_applied_state_range, so a change of local group, own country or a group's values alone makes the contact a changed contact on the normal path, with the same result as @FullRebuild (RULE-178); the local group and country lists are not reference inputs. (9) While the 'local_group_restatement' marker is present, the run takes the full path from 2020-10-01 and records adjustments at the own-country grain; its final transaction removes the marker (restatement by local group pattern). Its signature, parameters and step logging are unchanged. MOD-031's down script restores the MOD-028 definition.

entities.name: Layercake.usp_run_daily_load
entities.description: Existing Phase 1 daily run under one run_id, with its own 'run' row in etl_run_log. MOD-023 made it run Layercake.usp_run_payment_segments after the gold step, with the same run_id and no as-of date, so the attributes load uses the run date and one call populates Phase 1 and every segment column (RULE-123, RULE-124). MOD-029 changes its order (ADR-012, RULE-158): the Phase 1 bronze step; the Phase 1 silver step with the daily count held back; the Phase 1 gold step with the gold daily fact held back; usp_run_payment_segments; then usp_load_silv_daily_count, given the run's @FullRebuild and @RebuildFrom; then usp_load_fact_daily_member_count_detail. So the daily count uses the attributes loaded earlier in the same run, and every load still runs once. It opens no transaction of its own, as today. A failure in any step logs its run row 'Failed' and re-raises the original error to the caller. Steps that committed before the failure stay committed; a failed segment load also leaves that run's daily count and gold daily fact as the previous run left them. Running it again recovers with no manual step (RULE-125, RULE-158). Its parameters and its own logging are unchanged. MOD-029's down script restores the MOD-023 definition.

entities.name: Layercake.etl_daily_count_applied_contact

It holds one row per contact whose daily count inputs are held as last applied, with the silv_member_profile columns the derivation reads, as last applied. With the other four snapshot tables (etl_daily_count_applied_attribute from AMD-007), it holds exactly the rows and columns that the contact's etl_daily_count_input_basis fingerprint covers. A contact with a 'contact' basis row and no row here, or the reverse, means the stored figures may not match the snapshot, and the next run takes the full-recompute path from 2020-10-01. Only usp_load_silv_daily_count writes it. A run withdraws the rows (and the contacts' snapshot rows in the other four tables) of the contacts it is about to apply in its first batch transaction. Internal; no grant.
