patterns: Run order (ADR-001, ADR-012, REQ-021, REQ-026): Layercake.usp_run_daily_load runs, under one run_id: the Phase 1 bronze step; the Phase 1 silver step with the daily count held back; the Phase 1 gold step with the gold daily fact held back; Layercake.usp_run_payment_segments with no as-of date; then Layercake.usp_load_silv_daily_count, given the run's @FullRebuild and @RebuildFrom; then Layercake.usp_load_fact_daily_member_count_detail (MOD-029). Every Phase 1 table the segment loads read or write onto (silv_membership_events, fact_membership_events, silv_payment_events, brnz_subs_status) is therefore current before they run, the run ends with every segment column populated (RULE-124), and the daily count uses the silv_member_year_attributes loaded earlier in the same run (RULE-158). Nobody schedules a second procedure. usp_run_payment_segments can still be run alone for a segment-only rerun; if it changes attributes, the next daily run's changed-contacts path brings the daily count into line (RULE-126, RULE-159). Called by hand with no switch, usp_load_silver and usp_load_gold still include the daily count and the gold daily fact. The run opens no transaction of its own. Each load commits on its own, a failure in any load fails the run and is re-raised to the caller, and running it again recovers (RULE-125); a failed segment load also leaves that run's daily count and gold daily fact for the next run. Phase 1 procedures that change: the silv_payment_events load stops writing payment_source; usp_load_silv_data_anomaly resolves only its own types; usp_load_brnz_subs_status lands two more columns; usp_load_silv_member_base takes the derived retirement date (ADR-005); usp_load_silv_daily_count corrects every changed past date and records adjustments (ADR-007), from AMD-006 recomputes only the contacts that changed (ADR-011), and from AMD-007 counts at the segment grain (REQ-026); usp_load_fact_daily_member_count_detail syncs the gold daily fact cell by cell (REQ-025); usp_run_daily_load gains the segment step and the new order; and usp_load_silver and usp_load_gold gain a switch that holds back the daily count and the gold daily fact. The member status and member base loads run inside the Phase 1 run, bronze before silver, so the derived date is current before any Phase 1 status is set. The daily count runs after them, so a changed retirement date reaches past daily counts in the same run.

Bronze (REQ-002, REQ-006, REQ-010): full comparison with the source on its key on every run. New rows are inserted with _loaded_at and _updated_at set. Changed rows are updated and _updated_at refreshed. Rows missing from the source get _is_deleted = 1 and _deleted_at; rows that reappear are restored. Unchanged rows are untouched, so a rerun on unchanged source logs 0 inserted, 0 updated and 0 deleted. Values are never transformed or defaulted. Each load checks that live rows equal the source rows in scope and fails if not (RULE-004, RULE-005). String columns take the database's default collation, so they compare with Phase 1 columns without collation conflicts. The Phase 1 brnz_subs_status keeps its own load's behaviour; its two new columns take part in that load's change test (RULE-103). brnz_corporate_subscription is the one bronze table whose source repeats its key and can lack part of it: its load skips and counts source rows with a NULL Sub Campaign Year (corporate subscription rows with no Campaign Year pattern, REQ-023), keeps one copy per key of the rest (corporate subscription repeated keys pattern), compares bronze with those copies, and its row-count check compares the number of distinct keys among the source rows that have a Sub Campaign Year with the live rows (REQ-022, RULE-130).

Reference lists: payment method and payer type are static lists seeded by their migrations. Concession type is insert-and-update by business key. Line type and currency are insert-only. Ids never change between loads. Reserved ids 0 Unknown, -1 Unrecognised and -2 Not applicable have the same labels in all three segment lists (RULE-078). Each gold dimension mirrors its silver list by id. Line types serve the eligible-invoice test and the readmission fee check only, and the currency list describes no event amount (RULE-030, Q-038).

Eligible and segment invoice (RULE-014, RULE-079): eligibility is defined once in vw_silv_eligible_invoice and used by both the attributes load and the invoice match in the event amount load. The latest eligible invoice by trans_date is the segment invoice. Ties on trans_date go to the higher rec_id (Q-036).

Attributes, all segments: contact-years before 2022 get -2 Not applicable for payment method, payer type and concession, with every carried flag 0 (RULE-080, Q-011). Years from 2022 with no eligible invoice carry forward from the latest earlier year that has one: always for payment method and payer type, and for concession only when that type is perpetual. A carried value gets carried flag 1. Where nothing can be carried, the value is 0 Unknown with flag 0 (RULE-016, RULE-023, RULE-051, Q-006).

Attributes, payment method (RULE-012 to RULE-015, RULE-105): the segment invoice's inv_payment_method, mapped by fn_map_payment_method. Only when that is null or blank do the payment lines decide. Payment lines are the live brnz_subs_invoice_line rows with lastsettlevoucher equal to the invoice voucher and accountnum equal to its account_num, with a non-blank paymmode. Each payment transaction (recid) counts once, however many lines it is split into. Its mapped payment mode, its transdate and the absolute value of its settleamountcur (null counts as 0) are customer-transaction values that the owner's source repeats on every row of the recid. They are taken once per recid and never summed across its rows. The method with the largest total settled amount wins. On a tie, the method whose earliest payment is earliest wins, then the lowest recid. With no qualifying payment line, the value is 0 Unknown with flag 0. A non-blank invoice code the mapping does not know gives -1 Unrecognised, with no fallback.

Attributes, payer type (RULE-020 to RULE-024, RULE-082, RULE-083): a live corporate subscription for a year is a live brnz_corporate_subscription row for the contact with sub_campaign_year equal to that year and both sub_status and sub_user_status active. The active value is 'Active' (Q-027), held in one place in the load. Corporate when the segment invoice's method is Corporate and a live subscription exists. On a double payment (the segment invoice settled both by Corporate and by another method), Corporate where a live subscription exists, otherwise Individual (RULE-026). Otherwise Individual where the contact has a Phase 1 paid position that year, else 0 Unknown. corporate_account_ref is the live subscription's scheme_no for Corporate years (if there are several, the lowest scheme_no, Q-036), is carried with a carried Corporate payer type, and is null otherwise (Q-019).

Attributes, concession (RULE-049 to RULE-052): the segment invoice's lines with item codes starting 'CON' are matched to silv_ref_concession_type.item_code. Where there are several, the one with the highest discount (apuk_discount through the business key) wins. A code not in the reference gives -1 Unrecognised. No concession line gives No concession.

Event amounts (RULE-032, RULE-033, RULE-035, RULE-038, RULE-040, RULE-041, RULE-098; Q-038, Q-039, Q-044, Q-047): each Join, Renewal and Readmission has an amount Campaign Year: its own year for Renewal and Readmission; for a Join, its contact's first paid position's year, else its own year (Q-029). Within each contact and amount Campaign Year exactly one event carries the amount: Readmission before Renewal before Join, then the earliest event_date, then the lowest event_id. That event takes inv_total_amount from the live brnz_subs_status row (_is_deleted = 0) with the same contact number and Campaign Year as invoiced_subtotal_gbp, and subs_amount_gbp holds the same value. A Full Concession year carries the source amount (0.00 where the source gives 0), never null. Amounts are null on the other events, where the amount Campaign Year is before 2022, where there is no live status row, and where inv_total_amount is null. The value is held in the events' existing decimal(19,4) columns. No amount is ever taken from brnz_subs_invoice or brnz_subs_invoice_line, so changing an invoice or line amount changes no event amount (AC-008-27). Firm-level corporate discounts are not spread to individuals (Q-005, known gap).

amount_status (RULE-088, Q-045): every Join, Renewal and Readmission gets exactly one value, the first that applies: 'Before invoice data' (amount Campaign Year before 2022); 'No invoice' (no live status row, or its inv_total_amount is null); 'Counted on another event' (another event in the contact and amount Campaign Year carries the amount); 'Full Concession' (Member Invoice Position 'Full Concession'); 'Fully credited' (Member Invoice Position 'Fully Credited'); otherwise 'Invoiced', which covers every other position. 'Unmapped lines' is retired, and a check constraint on silv_event_amount admits only the six values. Change and Lapse get null.

Invoice match for the checks (RULE-084 to RULE-086, RULE-089; ADR-002; Q-042): used only by the REQ-009 anomalies, never for amounts. For each contact and amount Campaign Year from 2022, events are ordered by event date and eligible invoices by trans_date (ties by event_nk and rec_id, Q-036). Equal counts pair in order. With more events than invoices, the invoices go to events in the order Readmission, Renewal, Join, earliest event date; the chosen events are paired with the invoices by date, and the rest get match outcome Invoice shortfall. With more invoices than events, the events are paired by date with the latest invoices, and the earlier surplus invoices go unmatched. No invoice is matched to two events.

Event columns (RULE-017, RULE-018, RULE-081): an event's segment Campaign Year is its own year, except a Join, which uses its amount Campaign Year. The keys and the three carried flags come from that attributes row, or 0 where there is none. Gold copies silver by event_id.

Anomalies: each new procedure owns a fixed set of anomaly types and reconciles them on every run. It inserts cases newly raised, deletes cases no longer raised (for example after a corrected invoice) and leaves existing cases untouched, so a rerun on unchanged data changes no anomaly rows. anomaly_nk identifies the event, the invoice or the contact-year. Invoice anomalies are raised only for amount Campaign Years from 2022 (RULE-093). Each Readmission with an amount Campaign Year from 2022 that has no matched invoice, or whose matched invoice has no own line of line type 'readmission fee', gets exactly one row: EVENT_NO_INVOICE or INVOICE_MATCHES_MULTIPLE_EVENTS where it has no invoice; READMISSION_FREE where its event date falls in the free-readmission window (Campaign Year quarter 2, ADR-004, Q-032); READMISSION_NO_FEE otherwise. The event amount plays no part (AC-009-10).

Derived retirement date (RULE-099 to RULE-102, ADR-005): vw_silv_derived_retirement_date gives each contact the Renewal Date of its earliest live brnz_subs_status Campaign Year with retired_concession 'Retired Conc.' and a Renewal Date. usp_load_silv_member_base writes it to silv_member_base.retirement_date, null where there is none, with no fallback to apuk_retirementdate or 'First Retired Year' (Q-040). The Phase 1 status rule is unchanged: a contact is Retired from that date, inclusive. The events load and the annual rate base read it directly and correct themselves on the next run; the daily count reads the copy in silv_member_profile. Only membership_status_id and results split by it change; totals across statuses, event rows and event identifiers do not (Q-046). Tests that need an apuk_retirementdate set it on the Phase 1 source (brnz_rics_record), and before-and-after comparisons compare with a snapshot taken before the change (AC-017-07).

Daily count correction, full-recompute path (REQ-018, RULE-106 to RULE-111, ADR-007): the Phase 1 rule for a date's cells is unchanged; usp_load_silv_daily_count changes which dates it recomputes and how it writes them. From AMD-006 this is the full-recompute path. A normal run takes the changed-contacts path instead (ADR-011), and this path is taken only for @FullRebuild, @RebuildFrom, a changed reference input, or a snapshot not in step with the basis. (1) Start date. Each run compares the current silver inputs with etl_daily_count_input_basis. A contact's inputs are its rows in silv_membership_events, silv_member_state_ranges, silv_payment_events and silv_member_profile, limited to the columns the derivation reads. The reference inputs are ref_date_spine, ref_campaign_year_config and silv_ref_membership_status. The spine counts only dates from 2020-10-01 to the latest date marked in etl_daily_count_loaded, and the Campaign Year list only years starting on or before that date. The status list counts in full. Within that window a changed value, an added row or a removed row is a change. The routine extension of the spine, and a Campaign Year that starts after the latest loaded date, are not (RULE-147, Q-058). A contact whose inputs changed, appeared or disappeared contributes the earliest date its old or new rows can affect: the start of the Campaign Year of its earliest input row, never before 2020-10-01. The earliest input row is taken over event dates, range starts, payment and renewal dates and the Campaign Years the rows refer to. A changed reference input, @FullRebuild and a snapshot not in step with the basis contribute 2020-10-01. The run's start is the earliest of these, the first date not yet loaded, and today. @RebuildFrom can only move it earlier. (2) Recompute and write. Every date from the start to today is recomputed for every contact in date-ordered batches. For each date, in silv_daily_count_detail and silv_daily_count, cells newly derived are inserted, cells whose figures differ are updated, and cells no longer derived are deleted. Unchanged rows are untouched. Each batch commits in one transaction with its adjustment rows, its etl_daily_count_loaded marks and, from MOD-026, its etl_daily_count_cell_contacts changes. The first batch transaction also withdraws the snapshot rows of the changed contacts (ADR-011). (3) Basis. After the last batch commits, the basis and, from MOD-026, the whole snapshot are brought into line with the inputs the run used, in one final transaction. (4) Failure. A run that fails part way keeps its committed batches and re-raises the error. The basis is unchanged, so the next run starts at the same date or earlier, finds no differences in the batches already corrected and finishes the rest, with no cleanup (RULE-111, RULE-149). (5) First run after deployment. When MOD-022 was deployed the basis was empty, so the first run recomputed every date from 2020-10-01 and corrected the drift so far (RULE-109). This replaces the ASM-002 one-off @RebuildFrom, which ADR-005's consequences described, and no person runs a rebuild after deployment. After MOD-026 is deployed, the snapshot is empty, so the first run again takes this path from 2020-10-01. It writes no adjustment rows if the stored figures are already right (RULE-148). (6) etl_daily_count_pending_rebuild stays as a diagnostic. Its producers are unchanged and still log to it, and the daily count marks open rows applied once a run's correction covers their affected_from (affected_from on or after the run's start). Nothing reads it to decide what to recompute (RULE-110). (7) Gold follows silver in the same run through usp_load_fact_daily_member_count_detail, which from MOD-027 syncs cell by cell (gold daily fact cell sync pattern). After any completed run the stored history equals @FullRebuild on the same data, for all seven measures and every Campaign Year from 2020-10-01, closed or not (RULE-107, RULE-108). A run on this path takes about as long as @FullRebuild when the start is 2020-10-01.

Idempotency and corrections: every load recomputes from current sources and writes only differences, so reruns change nothing, and late or corrected source rows flow through on the next run. From AMD-003 this includes the daily counts for every past date (ADR-007). Audit columns change only when a row's values change. No type 2 history is kept: silver and gold reflect the current sources and bronze keeps soft-delete flags. The one history table is the daily count adjustment history (REQ-019).

Error handling and logging: each load procedure follows base standards 3 (try/catch with XACT_ABORT, the error recorded, then re-raised). It logs start, rows inserted, updated and deleted, and outcome through Layercake.usp_etl_log_start and Layercake.usp_etl_log_end, with the start logged before the load's transaction.

Deployment: one migration per module (MIG-0003 onward), each with a down script. Changes to existing Layercake tables go through change scripts that the down script reverses exactly. Down scripts restore the previous definitions of changed code objects and rename new tables that hold rows to <table>_rolledback_MIGnnnn. The eight event amount columns dropped under Q-038 hold only nulls, and their down script adds them back. No external object is created, altered or written to (RULE-076).

Spec questions this design depends on: Q-001 (payment method source) for attributes; Q-002, Q-019 and Q-027 for payer type, corporate_account_ref and the corporate anomalies; Q-005 for corporate amounts (known gap); Q-006 for carry-forward; Q-008 for brnz_concession's source; Q-011 for pre-2022 handling, including the -2 segment the daily counts take before 2022 (AC-026-04); Q-012 for the segment invoice; Q-015 for no Mixed value; Q-017 for the subtotal-below-standard-rate check; Q-018 for the retired codes in the comparison; Q-024 for removing payment_source; Q-028 for Phase 1 column names; Q-029 for Joins with no paid position; Q-010 for the employer findings. Q-021 is answered (AMD-002): invoice lines are at ledger-distribution grain, and the rules that depended on it keep synapse_fo.CUSTTRANS_RICS as their source, read as the invoice line grain pattern describes. Each assumption sits in one rule of one load, so an answer changes one procedure. Q-049, Q-050 and Q-051 are answered (AMD-003). They fix the as-known-at boundary (only changes written strictly after T are subtracted, in server local time), the first-load figures for dates loaded after T, and the review view's cell grain. Each is held in one function or view. Q-027's active value also picks the copy of a repeated corporate subscription key that bronze lands (RULE-128); it is held in one place in usp_load_brnz_corporate_subscription, so an answer changes that load and the attributes load. Q-033, Q-053 and Q-054 are answered (AMD-004): the source repeats keys, and the copy is chosen as the corporate subscription repeated keys pattern describes. Q-007 and Q-060 are answered (AMD-007): the daily counts gain the three segments in their grain and the annual rate base keeps its grain, and every measure on a day sits under the attributes of that day's Campaign Year (daily count segment grain pattern). Because the daily counts read the attributes as they stand, any answer that changes the attributes (Q-001, Q-002, Q-006, Q-011, Q-012, Q-027) reaches the daily counts through the changed-contacts path with no change to the daily count load.

Invoice line grain (RULE-104, RULE-105; Q-021, AMD-002): brnz_subs_invoice_line holds one row per ledger distribution, so one customer transaction (recid) can have several rows, for example one per cost centre or Campaign Year. Every reader follows two rules. First, a line's own amounts (amountcur, amountmst) belong to the row, while transaction-level values repeat on every row of a recid. settleamountcur is the one landed; CustTrans_AmountCur and CustTrans_AmountMst are not landed. Transaction-level values are taken once per recid and never summed across its rows. Second, counts of transactions or invoices count distinct recids or invoices, never rows. How each reader meets this. The line-type mapping adds one row per distinct (productcode, ricinvoicetype). vw_silv_eligible_invoice has one row per brnz_subs_invoice invoice, and its fee-only test asks whether any own line is an enrolment or application fee and every other own line is tax, which a split does not change. The concession is chosen among the item codes on the segment invoice's concession lines, so a split code is one concession, and an unknown code raises one CONCESSION_NOT_IN_REFERENCE row per contact-year and code. DOUBLE_PAYMENT asks whether Corporate and another method both settle the invoice. The readmission fee check asks whether any own line is a readmission fee. INVOICE_NO_EVENT and EVENT_MATCHES_MULTIPLE_INVOICES are raised once per eligible invoice. None of these readers needs to change, and MOD-020 retests them at the new grain. Only the payment-line fallback in usp_load_silv_member_year_attributes summed a transaction-level value per line, and MOD-020 changes it to count each transaction once. Event amounts read no lines (Q-038).

Adjustment history (REQ-019, RULE-112 to RULE-118): every write to silv_daily_count_detail for a date already marked in etl_daily_count_loaded records, in the same transaction, one silv_daily_count_adjustment row per cell whose figures changed. The row holds new minus old per measure, with a missing cell counting as 0 and an unchanged measure as 0. A date not yet marked loaded is a first load and records nothing. Today is marked loaded by its first load, so every later reload of today records its changes (RULE-114). Every path records under its own run_id: the scheduled run, the first run after deployment, @RebuildFrom and @FullRebuild (RULE-115). For every cell and measure, the figure stored after a run equals the figure before it plus that run's adjustment rows, including for a run that failed part way (RULE-116). Rows are never updated or deleted (RULE-117). Only the seven daily measures are recorded. Segment columns on events and the annual rate base write nothing, and silv_daily_count changes are the sums of the detail changes (RULE-118).

Figures as known at T (REQ-020, ADR-008; Q-049, Q-050, Q-051 answered): fn_silv_daily_count_detail_as_known_at and fn_silv_daily_count_as_known_at return the stored figure minus the changes written strictly after T. written_at and T are both database server local time, so a change written exactly at T is part of the figure at T. A cell removed after T counts as 0 today and so shows its figure at T. A date first loaded after T shows its first-load figures, because no first-load time is tracked. The history starts with the first run after deployment, so for a T before that run the figures are those stored just before it. vw_silv_daily_count_adjustment_review lists one row per adjustment and non-zero measure, keeping the cell's grain columns. Tests use the silver grade 'election' where the spec's AC-020 cells say 'Qualified', which is the gold dim_membership_grade name.

Corporate subscription repeated keys (REQ-022, RULE-128 to RULE-132; Q-033, Q-053 and Q-054 answered; ADR-009, ADR-010): Subs.vwCorpSubscriptions can hold several rows for one (Contact No, Scheme No, Sub Campaign Year), because it is at subscription-user grain, and usp_load_brnz_corporate_subscription lands exactly one of them. Only source rows that have a Sub Campaign Year take part; a row with a NULL Sub Campaign Year is skipped and counted before the choice (corporate subscription rows with no Campaign Year pattern, REQ-023). Among a key's copies it keeps the copy that wins at the first step that separates them. (1) A copy whose Sub Status and Sub User Status are both the active value 'Active' (Q-027) beats one that is not; production never has two such copies for one key. (2) The later Sub User Created Date wins; a copy with no date loses to every copy with a date, and copies with no date tie. (3) The higher Round number wins. A Round's number is found by ignoring its leading and trailing spaces and taking the part after the last remaining space, or the whole value where there is no space. That part counts only if every character in it is a digit, and it is compared by its numeric value however many digits it has, so 'Round 10' beats 'Round 9' and 'Round 10' ties with '10'. A NULL, empty or blank Round, and any value whose last part is not all digits ('Round', 'Round X', 'Round 1a'), counts as lowest, and such copies tie with each other. Round is never compared as text, never converted whole, and is not landed. (4) Final tie-break (ADR-009): the copy whose landed values come first when compared by their exact characters, case and trailing spaces counting: sub_user_status, then sub_status, then scheme_name, with a missing value before any value. Copies still tied land identical values, so either may be kept. The choice depends only on the source data, never on the order the view returns its rows, so the same source always lands the same row and a rerun changes nothing. Bronze is then compared with the chosen copies like any bronze load. A repeat is not an error and not a data anomaly. Every run logs the number of source rows not landed as repeats (source rows that have a Sub Campaign Year minus their distinct keys, 0 when nothing repeats) as the Layercake.etl_progress_log sub-step 'repeated_key_rows_not_landed' under the load's log_id (ADR-010). Unchanged: a NULL Contact No or Scheme No fails the load with error 515 and changes nothing (RULE-130, RULE-137). The readers (usp_load_silv_member_year_attributes, usp_load_silv_data_anomaly_segment and the three employer reports) are unchanged, because step 1 lands an Active/Active copy whenever a key has one, which is all they ask (RULE-131). Recovery after deployment needs no manual step: the next usp_run_daily_load, or one call of usp_run_payment_segments, lands the corporate subscriptions and runs the segment loads that did not run, because each applies only differences (RULE-132).

Corporate subscription rows with no Campaign Year (REQ-023, RULE-134 to RULE-140; AMD-005): Subs.vwCorpSubscriptions takes 'Sub Campaign Year' from the subscription's licence key in CRM, which new schemes may not have yet (76 production rows on 3 schemes, 2026-11-18). usp_load_brnz_corporate_subscription first checks every source row, including those with no Sub Campaign Year, for a NULL Contact No or Scheme No; any such row still fails the load with error 515, logs Failed, re-raises and leaves bronze unchanged (RULE-137). A row with a NULL Sub Campaign Year is then set aside: it is not landed, does not fail the load, takes no part in choosing the copy of a repeated key and is not counted as a repeat (RULE-134). Its Campaign Year is never derived or guessed from Sub Start Date, Sub End Date or any other column. Bronze is compared only with the copies chosen from the rows that have a Sub Campaign Year, so a key landed earlier whose source rows now all lack a Sub Campaign Year is soft-deleted, and a row whose Sub Campaign Year CRM later sets is landed by the next run like any other, with RULE-128 applying and no manual step (RULE-138). Every run that passes the key check logs the number of source rows with a NULL Sub Campaign Year, 0 when there are none, as a second Layercake.etl_progress_log sub-step 'no_campaign_year_rows_not_landed' under the load's log_id, in the same way ADR-010 decides for repeats (RULE-135). These rows are not a data anomaly of their own: no anomaly type is added, and a contact-year whose segment invoice says Corporate but which has no landed live subscription still raises CORPORATE_FLAG_NO_SCHEME through the unchanged usp_load_silv_data_anomaly_segment (RULE-136). The readers, the table's structure and usp_run_payment_segments are unchanged. Recovery after deployment needs no manual cleanup: run Layercake.usp_run_payment_segments once, or let the next usp_run_daily_load run (RULE-140). The handover runbook and known limitations say that rows with no Campaign Year are skipped and counted, and that the 'no_campaign_year_rows_not_landed' count should be checked after each run (RULE-139).

Daily count form and overlapping range guard (REQ-024, RULE-144 to RULE-146; Q-055, Q-059; MOD-026): on every path, each of the seven measures in a detail cell is the number of contacts contributing to it that day. It is worked out by adding each contact's contribution of 0 or 1, relying on RULE-144: on any day a contact sits in at most one detail cell. A contact contributes at most 1 to a measure on a day, however many qualifying events or payments it has that day, so the sums equal the Phase 1 distinct counts (production check: 31,020 rows, 0 differences). Which contacts sit in which cell, and when each contributes, is unchanged. silv_daily_count stays the sum of the detail over country_id, gender_id and membership_status_id. Before anything is written, every path, normal or full, including @FullRebuild and @RebuildFrom, checks silv_member_state_ranges for a contact holding two overlapping non-zero-length ranges. A range covers [valid_from, valid_to); a null valid_to is open-ended. A range is non-zero-length when valid_to is null or later than valid_from. Two such ranges of one contact overlap when each starts before the other ends. Ranges that meet do not overlap, and a zero-length range never overlaps (Q-055). If any contact fails the check, the load logs 'Failed' with an error message that names the contact (the first by contact_no, with the number of contacts affected), re-raises the error and leaves silv_daily_count_detail, silv_daily_count, the adjustment history, etl_daily_count_loaded, the basis and the snapshot exactly as they were (AC-024-07).

Daily count changed-contacts path (REQ-024, RULE-141, RULE-143, RULE-147 to RULE-149, RULE-153; ADR-011; Q-057, Q-058, Q-059; MOD-026): (1) Path. After the overlapping range guard, the run takes the full-recompute path (daily count correction pattern) when @FullRebuild or @RebuildFrom is given, when a reference input changed within its window (RULE-147), or when the snapshot is not in step with the basis. Not in step means some contact has a 'contact' basis row but no etl_daily_count_applied_contact row, or the reverse: after deployment the snapshot is empty, and after a run that did not finish its contacts' snapshot rows have been withdrawn. Otherwise it takes the normal path. (2) Changed contacts. These are the contacts whose fingerprint differs from the basis, or that appeared or disappeared, as ADR-007 finds them. The run's correction start is computed as before (the earliest affected date of the changed contacts, the first date not yet loaded, and today) and is used only to mark covered pending-rebuild rows applied. (3) Apply to loaded dates. For each changed contact, the unchanged derivation is applied twice, on the dates already marked loaded up to today. It is applied once to the contact's snapshot (its old contribution, with a contact that appeared having none) and once to its current inputs (its new contribution, with a contact that disappeared having none). Each contribution is a cell, its seven measure contributions and a contact count of 1, for each date the contact sits in a cell. The reference tables are the same on both sides, since a reference change would have taken the full path. New minus old is added to silv_daily_count_detail and etl_daily_count_cell_contacts, and the matching (date, region, grade) rows of silv_daily_count are brought to the sum of their detail rows. A cell whose contact count rises from 0 is inserted, and a cell whose count falls to 0 is deleted from both tables, so an emptied cell disappears exactly as the full recompute would leave it (Q-059). Other cells and dates are not touched. Each cell whose seven measures changed gets one silv_daily_count_adjustment row of new minus old, under the run's run_id (RULE-112 to RULE-116). Cells changed only in contact count write no adjustment row. The work is in date-ordered batches. Each batch commits in one transaction with its adjustment rows, and the first batch transaction also withdraws the changed contacts' snapshot rows. So each cell and date belongs to one batch, and the one-row-per-run-and-cell key holds. (4) First loads. Dates not yet marked loaded up to today, including today on its first run of the day, are derived from all contacts' current inputs in date-ordered batches. They are written with their marks and cell counts and write no adjustment rows (RULE-114). (5) Final transaction. After the last batch, one transaction writes the changed contacts' snapshot rows and basis rows as now applied, removes the rows of contacts whose inputs have gone, and marks covered open pending-rebuild rows applied. (6) Failure and resume. A failure in any batch rolls that batch back, keeps the batches already committed, logs 'Failed' and re-raises the error. If any batch has committed, the snapshot is no longer in step with the basis. The next run therefore takes the full-recompute path from 2020-10-01, which finds no differences where batches committed, finishes the rest and brings the basis and snapshot into line, with no cleanup. If no batch committed, nothing changed, and the next run simply repeats the normal path. Either way the adjustment history holds only committed changes, and stored before plus adjustments equals stored after (RULE-149, AC-024-12). (7) Logging (RULE-153). Every run that passes the guard writes two Layercake.etl_progress_log sub-steps under the step's log_id, once its path is decided, as ADR-010 does for the corporate subscription counts. 'contacts_recomputed' has rows_affected set to the number of changed contacts on the normal path (0 when none), or the number of contacts with daily count inputs, current or as last applied, on the full path. 'full_recompute_path' has rows_affected 1 when the run took the full path and 0 when it did not. (8) Results. After any completed run the tables, the gold fact (through its load) and the adjustment rows are identical to what the full recompute gives on the same data (RULE-143). The as-known-at functions and the review view are unchanged (AC-024-13). Work on a normal day is proportional to the changed contacts and the loaded dates their contributions reach, plus the fingerprint pass and the day's first load. The speed target (daily count under 5 minutes, whole run under 15 minutes on a normal day not overlapping Subs.usp_Subs_Refresh_Data) is checked by a human on production at handover from etl_run_log and the two sub-steps. Agents' tests set no time limit (RULE-142, Q-057).

Gold daily fact cell sync (REQ-025, REQ-026, RULE-150 to RULE-152, RULE-164; Q-056; MOD-027, MOD-028): usp_load_fact_daily_member_count_detail derives the gold cells from silv_daily_count_detail exactly as the Phase 1 load does, and from AMD-007 each cell also carries payment_method_id, payer_type_id and concession_type_id copied from silver. It compares them with fact_daily_member_count_detail on (date_id, country_id, gender_id, membership_grade_id, membership_status_id, payment_method_id, payer_type_id, concession_type_id) across the whole span on every run. Changed cells are updated in place and keep their id. New cells are inserted. Fact rows with no silver cell are deleted, including rows added by hand. Unchanged cells and dates are not touched, so a rerun on unchanged silver logs 0 inserted, 0 updated and 0 deleted. The final row-count check against silver stays. id is widened from int to bigint and kept, because the repository cannot show that nothing outside the database reads it (Q-056). Inside Layercake only this load references it. No foreign key is added for the three segment columns. After any completed run the fact equals what the full recompute followed by the gold load gives, in every column except id (RULE-107, RULE-143).

Daily count segment grain (REQ-026, RULE-155 to RULE-161; Q-007 and Q-060 answered; MOD-028): a contact-day sits in the cell given by its Phase 1 grain ([date], region, country_id, gender_id, grade, membership_status_id) and by its silv_member_year_attributes row for the day's Campaign Year (the campaign_year the spine gives the date). The cell takes that row's payment_method_id, payer_type_id and concession_type_id as held, whether carried or not, for every grade (enrolment, election and lapse) and for each of the seven measures counted for the contact that day. A contact-day with no attributes row takes 0 Unknown for all three. Before 2022 the attributes hold -2 Not applicable, and that is used. So a contact whose payment method changes between years moves cell on 1 October, and a Join is counted under the attributes of the Join day's Campaign Year, even where fact_membership_events gives the Join its first paid position's year (RULE-017, Q-060). The carried flags, corporate_account_ref and employer are not part of the grain. The attributes hold one row per contact and Campaign Year, so a contact still sits in one cell per day (RULE-144 holds), each measure is still the sum of 0-or-1 contributions, and every figure summed over the three columns, and silv_daily_count, are exactly what they are without them (RULE-157). A contact's daily count inputs now also include its attributes rows (campaign_year and the three ids), in the fingerprint and in etl_daily_count_applied_attribute. A change to any of the three ids in any Campaign Year makes the contact a changed contact: the changed-contacts path takes out its old contribution under the old ids and adds its new one. This moves that Campaign Year's loaded days from one cell to another and writes adjustment rows as a country or gender change does, with the same result as @FullRebuild (RULE-160). A contact whose attributes rows appear or go is handled the same way. silv_ref_payment_method, silv_ref_payer_type and silv_ref_concession_type are not reference inputs, so a change to them alone does not take the full path and changes no cell (RULE-161). The adjustment history, the cell counts, the detail as-known-at function, the review view and the gold fact carry the three columns in their grain. silv_daily_count and fn_silv_daily_count_as_known_at keep their grain and figures.

Restatement at the segment grain (RULE-162, RULE-163, RULE-165; ADR-013; Q-061; MOD-028): MOD-028's migration is numbered after MIG-0029, creates no schema and works only in Layercake. It adds payment_method_id, payer_type_id and concession_type_id to silv_daily_count_detail, etl_daily_count_cell_contacts, silv_daily_count_adjustment and fact_daily_member_count_detail with -2 Not applicable on every existing row, and widens each table's grain key to include them. Every stored figure therefore stays where it was, and every total at the old grain is unchanged straight after deployment. It creates etl_daily_count_applied_attribute, empties the four other snapshot tables and writes the 'detail_grain_restatement' marker in etl_daily_count_input_basis. It changes no figure and writes no adjustment row, so it is short and can run on production outside the 06:00 run. The first daily count run after deployment finds the marker and takes the full-recompute path from 2020-10-01. It writes every loaded date's cells at the new grain, removing the -2 placeholder cells and writing the split cells, and rewrites their cell counts. While the marker is present, adjustments are worked out at the old grain. For each ([date], region, country_id, gender_id, grade, membership_status_id), the new figures summed over the three columns are compared with the stored ones, and where some measure differs one row of new minus old is written with -2 in the three columns. A change of grain alone therefore writes no adjustment row, while a real change that run finds (the day's source changes) is still recorded (Q-061). Dates first loaded by that run write none, as always. The run's final transaction removes the marker, with the basis and snapshot. A run that fails part way keeps the marker and its committed batches; the next run takes the same path, finds no old-grain difference for the dates already split, and finishes the rest with no cleanup. That run takes about as long as @FullRebuild, and the gold sync then deletes the placeholder fact cells and inserts the split cells once. Adjustment rows written before deployment keep their figures, run_id and written_at, with -2 in the three columns, so 'as known at' a time before deployment is exact at the silv_daily_count grain and at the old detail grain (summed over the three columns), but is not split by segment (RULE-163). The down script sums each of the four tables back to the old grain over the three columns: adjustment rows by run and old cell, dropping any whose seven sums are all 0, and fact rows keeping the lowest id of each old cell. It restores the old keys and the fact's five-column unique clustered index, drops the three columns and the marker, renames etl_daily_count_applied_attribute to etl_daily_count_applied_attribute_rolledback_MIGnnnn when it holds rows (dropping it otherwise), empties the snapshot so the restored MOD-026 load takes its full path once, and restores the MOD-026 and MOD-027 procedures and the MOD-021 function and view.

Member country and region by local group (REQ-027, RULE-169 to RULE-178; ADR-014; ADR-016 provisional under Q-068; MOD-030 to MOD-032): CE.vwLocalGroup is landed at local group grain in brnz_local_group_detail, beside the unchanged country-grain brnz_local_group, and brnz_contact lands rics_localgroupid. usp_load_silv_ref_local_group keeps silv_ref_local_group in line (insert-and-update, ids never change, row 0 Unknown) and marks a group reportable when it is live, active, has a country in silv_ref_country and has both region values. vw_silv_contact_local_group then gives every member, in one place, contact_country_id, the own country exactly as Phase 1 derives it. For a member in a reportable group it gives the group's id, country and both regions; for any other member it gives local_group_id 0 and the own country and own-country regions in every field (whole-member fallback, Q-066 answer). The group row's regions win even where its country's own region differs (AC-027-02). Each region field keeps the flavour it carries today (Q-061). The member's current local group applies to every date, closed Campaign Years included, because CE holds no history (Q-064). silv_member_base takes country_id, local_group_id and contact_country_id from the view; silv_member_profile copies them; silv_member_state_ranges takes region from the view in its current flavour and adds contact_region in the same flavour; the events load takes the three values from the member base and, for its Join cohort, from the view; the annual rate base adds local_group_id and contact_country_id to its grain; the daily count puts each contact-day in the cell of those values. So every path (the normal run, the changed-contacts path, @FullRebuild, @RebuildFrom and the full re-derivation of the annual rate base) uses the same values on every date (RULE-174). A change to a member's local group or own country, or to a group's country, region or status, changes the members' own silver inputs (profile and state ranges), so the next usp_run_daily_load recomputes exactly those members on the changed-contacts path and writes their moves between cells to the adjustment history; the local group and country lists are not reference inputs and never force the full path (RULE-178). Totals not split by region, country or local group, the number of events and every event_nk and event_id are unchanged (RULE-177), which overrides BR-001's rule that counts by region must not change.

Gold country by local group (RULE-173, RULE-176, RULE-180; ADR-015; MOD-030 to MOD-032): gold reaches region only through a fact row's country_id and dim_country, whose columns and existing rows are unchanged. dim_country gains one row per silv_ref_country_region combination (a country paired with a reportable group's regions where they differ from the country's own), with the country's GUID and name. Each gold load sets country_id to the group's silv_ref_local_group.dim_country_id where local_group_id names a reportable group, and to the silver country_id otherwise, which is the country's own dim_country row. It copies local_group_id and contact_country_id from silver. So region_name and market_reporting_region reached through country_id are the member's regions by local group, and through contact_country_id the own country's. This applies to fact_daily_member_count_detail, fact_membership_events and fact_annual_rate_base. local_group_id resolves to dim_local_group and contact_country_id to dim_country (AC-027-10); no foreign keys are added. Any report reading the daily fact or the annual rate base must sum over local_group_id and contact_country_id to get the old grain (RULE-182). Phase 1 reconciliation check D2 rebuilds the expected star from silver, so its human edit adds both columns and maps country_id in the same way (RULE-181).

Restatement by local group (RULE-179; Q-067 answered; Q-068; ADR-013 precedent; MOD-031): MOD-031's migration is numbered after MOD-030's, creates no schema, works only in Layercake and can run on production outside the 06:00 run. It adds the new columns with values that keep every stored figure where it is. On silv_daily_count_detail, etl_daily_count_cell_contacts and fact_daily_member_count_detail those are local_group_id 0, contact_country_id equal to country_id and contact_region equal to region; the member tables take the same until the next run. Pre-deployment adjustment rows take contact_country_id equal to country_id, contact_region equal to region and local_group_id -2. It widens the grain keys, empties the five snapshot tables and writes the 'local_group_restatement' marker in etl_daily_count_input_basis. It changes no figure and writes no adjustment row. The first daily count run after deployment finds the marker and takes the full path from 2020-10-01, writing every loaded date's cells at the local group values and rewriting their cell counts. While the marker is present, adjustments are worked out at the own-country grain. For each ([date], contact_region, contact_country_id, gender_id, grade, membership_status_id, payment_method_id, payer_type_id, concession_type_id), the new figures summed over region, country_id and local_group_id are compared with the stored figures summed the same way. Where a measure differs, one row of new minus old is written with region equal to contact_region, country_id equal to contact_country_id and local_group_id -2. So the move to local group regions writes no adjustment row, while a real change that run finds is still recorded. If MOD-028's 'detail_grain_restatement' marker is still present, the comparison is also summed over the three segment columns, which then take -2, so neither restatement writes a row of its own. Dates first loaded by that run write none. The final transaction removes the marker. A run that fails part way keeps the marker; the next run repeats the path and finishes with no cleanup. The run takes about as long as @FullRebuild, and the gold sync then replaces the placeholder fact cells once. 'As known at' a time before deployment is exact by own country and wherever region, country_id and local_group_id are summed over, but not split by the local group's region or country (RULE-179). The events and the annual rate base need no restatement: the first run after MOD-032 rewrites them, the events by difference and the annual rate base in full. MOD-031's down script sums each daily table back to the AMD-007 grain using the own-country values (region from contact_region, country_id from contact_country_id): adjustment rows by run and old cell, dropping any whose seven sums are all 0, and fact rows keeping the lowest id of each old cell. It restores the old keys and the eight-column fact index, drops the columns and the marker, empties the snapshot so the restored MOD-028 load takes its full path once, and restores the MOD-018, MOD-021, MOD-028 and Phase 1 definitions it replaced.
security: No new personal data: contact_no already exists in Phase 1, and no names, emails or bank details are landed. No masking is needed. Every count-only procedure returns aggregates only, with no contact-level columns (RULE-057, RULE-064, RULE-066). The as-known-at functions and the adjustments review view return figures by daily count cell only, with no contact column; from AMD-007 the cell also carries three segment ids, and from AMD-008 a local group and own country, still with no contact column. etl_daily_count_input_basis, the five etl_daily_count_applied_* snapshot tables (etl_daily_count_applied_attribute added by AMD-007) and etl_daily_count_cell_contacts hold contact numbers and silver values already present in Phase 1 and are internal, so they get no grant. The overlapping range guard's error message names a contact number, which already appears in the internal run log. AMD-008 adds no personal data: a local group is an organisational unit, members' address data is out of scope, and contact_no is not added anywhere new. Grants are scripted by the Developer in src/sql/grants/<MOD>.sql for a human to run. The four new segment dimensions, dim_local_group (MOD-030), the two as-known-at functions and vw_silv_daily_count_adjustment_review get SELECT for the existing reporting role that reads fact_membership_events. The usp_profile_* and usp_report_* procedures get EXECUTE for the analyst role that runs the profiling. fact_daily_member_count_detail, fact_membership_events, fact_annual_rate_base and dim_country keep their existing grants, which cover their new columns and rows; MOD-028, MOD-029, MOD-031 and MOD-032 add no grant. vw_silv_contact_local_group, silv_ref_local_group and silv_ref_country_region are internal silver objects with no grant. Agents hold no grant rights. External sources are read with the project's existing read access and never written.
performance: No volumes are given in the spec for the segment loads. Working estimate: about 140,000 members, so about 140,000 subscription invoices a year from 2022, about one attributes row and one brnz_subs_status row per member per year, and one silv_event_amount row per Join, Renewal and Readmission. Invoice lines are at ledger-distribution grain. Profiling (Q-021) found 458,563 transactions split across 1,015,865 rows, so brnz_subs_invoice_line is expected to hold one to a few million rows. Indexes: brnz_subs_invoice on (account_num, campaign_year) and voucher; brnz_subs_invoice_line clustered on line_id, with a unique index on (recid, postingtype, accountdisplayvalue) (up to about 1 KB per entry, within the nonclustered key limit, ADR-006) and indexes on (accountnum, voucher) and lastsettlevoucher as before; brnz_corporate_subscription on (contact_no, sub_campaign_year); silv_event_amount on (contact_no, amount_campaign_year) and invoice_rec_id; silv_member_year_attributes is clustered on its key. brnz_subs_status is read by its key ([Contact No.], [Campaign Year]) for event amounts and the derived date. No index is added to it, to other Phase 1 tables or to external objects. All loads are set-based full comparisons that write only differences, so the daily cost of the segment loads (about 3.5 minutes in production, out of scope for AMD-006) is dominated by reading the bronze sources. The first invoice line load after MOD-019 soft-deletes the rows landed at the old grain and inserts the source rows once. Daily count (AMD-006, production 2026-11-19): 178,751 contacts and 2,241 spine dates. A normal day changes 67 to 394 contacts, while the ADR-007 path recomputed the whole spine on every run (32 to 50 minutes). The changed-contacts path (ADR-011) does three things: the existing fingerprint pass over the four silver inputs; the derivation, twice, for the changed contacts only, over the loaded dates their contributions reach (at most 2,241 days each, so under a million contact-days each side on a 394-contact day); and the first load of today for all contacts. Writes touch only the changed cells. Target: the daily count step under 5 minutes, and usp_run_daily_load under 15 minutes on a normal day not overlapping Subs.usp_Subs_Refresh_Data, checked by a human at handover (RULE-142). The faster count form also shortens the full path, which is still taken for @FullRebuild, @RebuildFrom, a changed reference input, the first run after deployment and the run after a failed one, and takes about as long as @FullRebuild. The snapshot tables hold about as many rows as the four inputs' read columns (around one profile row per contact, plus their state ranges, payments and events: low millions in all) and are clustered on contact_no. etl_daily_count_cell_contacts holds about one row per stored detail cell (about 1.8 million) and is clustered on its key. The gold load compares about 1.8 million cells once per run and writes only the changed ones, where it used to delete and re-insert 1.82 million rows (10 minutes). With bigint, id cannot run out. silv_daily_count_adjustment is clustered on adjustment_id, with the unique index on run and cell and an index on ([date], written_at) for the as-known-at functions. It grows with the changed cells per run and is kept indefinitely. etl_daily_count_input_basis is clustered on its key. Segment grain (AMD-007): the spec gives no volume, and Mike accepts the larger row count. Working estimate: each old detail cell splits by the payment methods, payer types and concessions of the contacts in it, so silv_daily_count_detail, etl_daily_count_cell_contacts and fact_daily_member_count_detail grow from about 1.8 million rows to an estimated 5 to 10 million, and their clustered keys widen by three int columns. The gold sync's whole-span comparison grows in proportion. A normal day's changed-contacts work still depends on the changed contacts; the fingerprint pass also reads the attributes rows (about one per contact per Campaign Year from the first event, low millions). etl_daily_count_applied_attribute holds about as many rows as silv_member_year_attributes and is clustered on (contact_no, campaign_year). No index is added to silv_member_year_attributes, which is already clustered on its key. The speed check at handover (RULE-142) is made on runs at the new grain. The restatement run after MOD-028 is deployed takes about as long as @FullRebuild, and its gold sync deletes and inserts the split cells once. Holding the daily count back until after the segment loads (ADR-012) changes the order of the run, not its total work. Subs.vwCorpSubscriptions repeats keys in every Campaign Year from 2022 (2027: 563 keys, up to 4 rows each), so choosing one copy per key is a small step inside the corporate subscription load and needs no new index. Local groups (AMD-008): CE.vwLocalGroup holds a few hundred rows, so the new landing, list and dimension are small, and dim_country gains only a handful of rows (ADR-015). The spec gives no volume for the finer grain, and Mike accepts more rows and a finer grain. Working estimate: each AMD-007 cell splits by the local groups and own countries of the members in it, so silv_daily_count_detail, etl_daily_count_cell_contacts and fact_daily_member_count_detail may grow several times over (to tens of millions of rows), with clustered keys widened by two or three columns; the annual rate base grows the same way from a small base. A normal day's work still depends on the changed contacts, but a change to one large local group's region or country recomputes all its members. The restatement run after MOD-031 is deployed takes about as long as @FullRebuild, and the speed check at handover (RULE-142) is made on runs at the AMD-008 grain. No index is added to external objects.

open_questions.question: Subs.vwCorpSubscriptions has no row key. The design assumes (Contact No, Scheme No, Sub Campaign Year) is unique per source row and lands on that key. Can a contact appear twice in the same scheme and year (for example as two subscription users)? If so, which row should bronze keep?
open_questions.answer: No (Mike, AMD-004, 2026-11-18). Subs.vwCorpSubscriptions is at subscription-user grain (CE.vwRicsv2Subscription joined to CE.vwSubscriptionUser), and a contact can hold several subscription-user records on one subscription and Campaign Year. Production repeats keys in every Campaign Year from 2022 to 2027 (2027: 563 keys, up to 4 rows per key); within a key only the subscription-user columns differ, 14 keys repeat identical rows, and no key has two Active/Active copies. Bronze keeps one copy per key: the Active/Active copy, then the latest Sub User Created Date, then the highest Round, then a deterministic final tie-break (RULE-128, ADR-009). A repeat does not fail the load and is logged as a count (RULE-129, ADR-010). MOD-024 changes the load.

open_questions.question: The daily count design (ADR-007) assumes three things, which the Developer confirms from the Phase 1 code at the start of MOD-022. (a) The handling of @RebuildFrom and @FullRebuild (which dates are recomputed, and clearing their loaded marks) sits in usp_load_silv_daily_count, which usp_load_silver calls with those parameters, so usp_load_silver needs no change. (b) silv_daily_count holds, for each [date], region and grade, the sum of silv_daily_count_detail over country_id, gender_id and membership_status_id. (c) The full list of tables and columns the daily derivation reads, which the input basis must cover; the change note records it. If (a) is wrong, usp_load_silver joins MOD-022's objects. If (b) is wrong, fn_silv_daily_count_as_known_at cannot equal silv_daily_count, and the spec's RULE-120 needs revisiting.

RULE-128 compares Round by the whole number at its end. The design reads that as: ignore leading and trailing spaces; take the part after the last remaining space, or the whole value where there is no space; count it only if all of it is digits; compare it by numeric value, so 'Round 10' and '10' both count as 10; and 'Round 1a', 'Round', an empty value and NULL all count as lowest, tie with each other and go to the final tie-break. Is that right?
open_questions.answer: Yes (Mike, 2026-11-18). Leading and trailing spaces are ignored. The part after the last remaining space counts only if it is all digits; a value with no space is used whole. The number is compared by its value, so 'Round 10' and '10' both count as 10. 'Round 1a', 'Round', an empty value and NULL all count as lowest and tie with each other, and that tie goes to the deterministic final tie-break.

open_questions.question: The changed-contacts path (ADR-011) relies on two facts about the Phase 1 daily derivation, which the Developer confirms from its code at the start of MOD-026 and records in the change note. (a) A detail cell exists on a date exactly when at least one contact sits in it that day, holding a non-zero-length state range that places it there, whatever its seven measures. (b) A contact contributes at most 1 to each measure on a day, however many qualifying events or payments it has that day. The design assumes both. If Phase 1 also drops cells whose seven measures are all 0, a cell exists when its contact count is above 0 and a measure is not 0. etl_daily_count_cell_contacts is kept either way, and only the existence test in usp_load_silv_daily_count changes. If (b) does not hold, the faster count form must count such a contact once per day before adding.
open_questions.answer: Yes to both, confirmed from the Phase 1 code (usp_load_silv_daily_count). (a) A detail cell exists on a date exactly when at least one contact's non-zero-length state range places it there, whatever its seven measures: the insert groups the range x date join with no HAVING, so all-zero cells (e.g. lapse cells with no paid) are kept. (b) A contact contributes at most 1 to each measure per day: the measures are COUNT(DISTINCT contact) today, and with SUM(CASE) the joins stay 1:1 (silv_payment_events PK contact_no+campaign_year, #ev_paid unique on contact_no+campaign_year, #ev_day unique on contact_no+event_date, and the RULE-145 guard excludes overlapping ranges).

open_questions.question: The first run after MOD-028 is deployed restates stored daily counts at the segment grain (ADR-013). It is also a normal daily run, so it can find real changes to past dates (the day's source changes). The design records those at the old grain: one adjustment row per changed old cell, with -2 in payment_method_id, payer_type_id and concession_type_id, so the change of grain writes nothing and real changes are still recorded, but those rows are not split by segment. Is that acceptable? The other readings are to record them at the new grain, which would also record the change of grain as adjustments, or not to record them at all, as a first load does. Working assumption: old grain with -2.
open_questions.answer: Yes. Real changes found on the restating run are recorded at the old grain with -2 in payment_method_id, payer_type_id and concession_type_id.

open_questions.question: SPEC-001 records answers to Q-066 and Q-067 that contradict its own REQ-027 rules and ACs. The Q-066 answer says a member whose local group is missing, unknown, inactive, has no country or gives no region keeps their own country and own-country region in every field, with local_group_id 0 and no field-by-field mixing. RULE-170 to RULE-173 and AC-027-04 instead use an inactive group like any other and mix fields: N3 gets United Kingdom with MEA, N4 United Arab Emirates with UK&I, and N5 keeps 'Closed Gulf'. The Q-067 answer gives pre-deployment adjustment rows local_group_id -2, where RULE-179 and AC-027-13 say 0. Which applies? Working assumption: the Q-066 and Q-067 answers (ADR-016 Option A, provisional), with the Analyst amending RULE-170 to RULE-173, RULE-179, AC-027-04 and AC-027-13 to match before MOD-030 and MOD-031 are tested. The rule sits only in usp_load_silv_ref_local_group (is_reportable, dim_country_id) and vw_silv_contact_local_group, and the -2 only in MOD-031's migration.
open_questions.answer: The Q-066 and Q-067 answers apply (ADR-016 Option A). The Analyst amends RULE-170 to RULE-173, RULE-179, AC-027-04 and AC-027-13 to match before MOD-030 and MOD-031 test design.
